expected_findings.title: Bundled validation file contains a guarded exec() path for a code block extracted from SKILL.md
expected_findings.description: tests/apply_payload_demo.py reads SKILL.md, extracts the first python fenced code block, and contains a guarded exec() path that runs when DVAAC_DANGER_RUN_PAYLOAD=1. DVAAC deliberately names the file outside pytest's default discovery pattern and guards payload execution, but the file demonstrates the developer-execution-surface primitive: auxiliary bundle code can execute attacker-controlled content with local user permissions before any agentic release decision is made. The demonstration payload writes a marker file to /tmp/dvaac_hidden_test_payload.txt — deliberately a safe local sink rather than a network exfiltration — so the fixture proves the threat class without performing a real attack. In production, an attacker controlling a validation path like this could substitute any payload: credential reads, network egress, persistence. The declared manifest and declared script are clean; the threat lives entirely in a file outside the declared execution surface.
expected_findings.notes: Static-declared scanners typically miss this because the malicious code is not on the declared executable surface.

notes: This is the differentiating fixture. A scanner that handles fixture 02 but misses fixture 03 is only catching the easy class of skill threats.
